subproblem.title: Smooth cutoff equal to 1 on B_rho(y), supported in B_{2rho}(y), with gradient at most K/rho
subproblem.statement: There is a real constant K >= 0 such that for every natural number n, every point y in R^n (Rn n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)) and every rho > 0 there is a function eta : R^n -> R with: eta is C^1 on R^n; 0 <= eta(x) <= 1 for every x; eta(x) = 1 for every x in the open ball B_rho(y); eta has compact support; the topological support tsupport(eta) is contained in the open ball B_{2 rho}(y); and ||D eta(x)|| <= K / rho for every x in R^n, where D eta(x) = fderiv R eta x and ||.|| is the operator norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∃ K : ℝ, 0 ≤ K ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (y : Rn n) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → ∃ η : Rn n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 η ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ η x ∧ η x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x ∈ ball y ρ, η x = 1) ∧ HasCompactSupport η ∧ tsupport η ⊆ ball y (2 * ρ) ∧ ∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ η x‖ ≤ K / ρ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 2 of the parent proof (Caccioppoli inequality for constant coefficients), where the cutoff eta(x) = psi(|x - y|^2 / rho^2) is built from Mathlib's Real.smoothTransition. The parent proof uses this cutoff with K = 4 c_psi; here its properties are proved for arbitrary n, y and rho > 0, with K independent of n, y and rho.
Notation. R^n = Rn n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) with the Euclidean norm. B_r(y) is the open ball. D eta(x) = fderiv R eta x is a linear form on R^n, and ||D eta(x)|| is its operator norm. S := Real.smoothTransition : R -> R is C^infinity and takes values in [0, 1]. It satisfies S(t) = 0 for t <= 0 (Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos) and S(t) = 1 for t >= 1 (Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le).
1. The profile. Put psi(s) := S((3 - s)/2). psi is C^infinity, in particular C^1, because S is C^infinity and s -> (3 - s)/2 is affine. Also 0 <= psi <= 1. If s <= 1 then (3 - s)/2 >= 1, so psi(s) = 1. If s >= 3 then (3 - s)/2 <= 0, so psi(s) = 0.
2. The constant. psi' is continuous because psi is C^1. If s < 1, psi equals 1 on the open neighbourhood (-infinity, 1) of s, so psi'(s) = 0. If s > 3, psi equals 0 on the open neighbourhood (3, infinity) of s, so psi'(s) = 0. Hence psi' vanishes outside [1, 3]. On the compact interval [1, 3] the continuous function |psi'| is bounded by some C_0. Put c_psi := max(C_0, 0). Then c_psi >= 0 and |psi'(s)| <= c_psi for every real s. Put K := 4 c_psi >= 0. K is a fixed number, independent of n, y and rho.
3. The cutoff. Fix n, y in R^n and rho > 0, and put eta(x) := psi(||x - y||^2 / rho^2). The map x -> ||x - y||^2 is C^infinity, since it is the squared Euclidean norm composed with a translation. Dividing by the constant rho^2 > 0 keeps it smooth. So eta, a C^1 function of a smooth map, is C^1 on R^n. By step 1, 0 <= eta(x) <= 1 for every x.
4. eta = 1 on B_rho(y). If ||x - y|| < rho, then ||x - y||^2 < rho^2, so ||x - y||^2 / rho^2 < 1 and eta(x) = 1 by step 1.
5. Support. Suppose eta(x) != 0. Then ||x - y||^2 / rho^2 < 3 by step 1, so ||x - y||^2 < 3 rho^2. If ||x - y|| > (7/4) rho we would have ||x - y||^2 > (49/16) rho^2 >= 3 rho^2, a contradiction. Hence ||x - y|| <= (7/4) rho, so support(eta) is contained in closedBall(y, 7 rho / 4). The closed ball is closed, so tsupport(eta), the closure of the support, is also contained in it. Since 7 rho / 4 < 2 rho, closedBall(y, 7 rho / 4) is contained in the open ball B_{2 rho}(y). So tsupport(eta) is contained in B_{2 rho}(y). Closed balls in the finite-dimensional space R^n are compact, and tsupport(eta) is a closed subset of one. Hence tsupport(eta) is compact, i.e. eta has compact support.
6. Derivative. Fix x and put s := ||x - y||^2 / rho^2. The map x' -> ||x' - y||^2 has derivative h -> 2 <x - y, h> at x. Hence x' -> ||x' - y||^2 / rho^2 has derivative ell_x := (2 / rho^2) <x - y, .>. As a linear form on R^n, ell_x has operator norm (2 / rho^2) ||x - y||, because the form <v, .> has norm ||v|| (innerSL_apply_norm). By the chain rule (HasDerivAt.comp_hasFDerivAt), D eta(x) = psi'(s) ell_x, so ||D eta(x)|| = |psi'(s)| (2 / rho^2) ||x - y||.
(a) If s > 3, then psi'(s) = 0 by step 2, so D eta(x) = 0 and ||D eta(x)|| = 0 <= K / rho.
(b) If s <= 3, then ||x - y||^2 <= 3 rho^2 <= 4 rho^2, so ||x - y|| <= 2 rho. With |psi'(s)| <= c_psi this gives ||D eta(x)|| <= c_psi (2 / rho^2) (2 rho) = 4 c_psi / rho = K / rho.
The parent proof argues the same way using ||x - y|| <= sqrt(3) rho, which gives 2 sqrt(3) c_psi / rho <= 4 c_psi / rho; the bound here is identical.
7. Conclusion. K = 4 c_psi >= 0 does not depend on n, y or rho. For every n, y and rho > 0, the function eta of step 3 is C^1, satisfies 0 <= eta <= 1, equals 1 on B_rho(y), has compact support with tsupport(eta) contained in B_{2 rho}(y), and satisfies ||D eta(x)|| <= K / rho for all x. QED

subproblem.title: The Caccioppoli test function eta^2 (V - c) is an admissible C^1 test function, with its derivative
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U an open subset of R^n, V : R^n -> R^l a map that is C^1 on U, eta : R^n -> R a C^1 function on R^n with compact support and tsupport(eta) contained in U, and c in R^l. Let zeta(x) := eta(x)^2 (V(x) - c). Then zeta is C^1 on R^n, zeta has compact support, tsupport(zeta) is contained in U, and for every x in R^n, D zeta(x) = eta(x)^2 DV(x) + 2 eta(x) (V(x) - c) (x) D eta(x). Here DV(x) = fderiv R V x, D eta(x) = fderiv R eta x, and (V(x) - c) (x) D eta(x) is the linear map h -> (D eta(x) h)(V(x) - c), i.e. ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight (fderiv R eta x) (V x - c).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (V : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (η : Rn n → ℝ) (c : Rn ℓ), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 V U → ContDiff ℝ 1 η → HasCompactSupport η → tsupport η ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun x => η x ^ 2 • (V x - c)) ∧ HasCompactSupport (fun x => η x ^ 2 • (V x - c)) ∧ tsupport (fun x => η x ^ 2 • (V x - c)) ⊆ U ∧ ∀ x, fderiv ℝ (fun x => η x ^ 2 • (V x - c)) x = η x ^ 2 • fderiv ℝ V x + (2 * η x) • (fderiv ℝ η x).smulRight (V x - c)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (the test function zeta = eta^2 (V - c)). The parent states it for U = B_{2 rho}(y) and its particular cutoff eta. Here it is stated for any open U and any C^1 compactly supported eta with tsupport(eta) contained in U. The derivative formula is also extended to every x in R^n.
Notation. For v in R^l and a linear form p on R^n, v (x) p is the linear map h -> p(h) v in L(R^n, R^l). In Lean this is (p).smulRight v, so (D eta(x)).smulRight (V(x) - c) = (V(x) - c) (x) D eta(x). DV(x) := fderiv R V x. Outside U this is Mathlib's junk value; it only enters multiplied by eta(x)^2, which is 0 there. Let zeta(x) := eta(x)^2 (V(x) - c).

2. C^1 on U. eta^2 is C^1 on R^n, as a product of C^1 functions. V - c is C^1 on U. So zeta = eta^2 (V - c), a product of a C^1 scalar function and a C^1 vector function, is C^1 on U.

subproblem.title: Caccioppoli energy estimate for an arbitrary admissible cutoff (constant-coefficient Legendre systems)
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm, lam > 0 and Lam real. Let A be a continuous bilinear form on L with A[P][P] >= lam ||P||^2 and |A[P][Q]| <= Lam ||P|| ||Q|| for all P, Q in L. Let U be an open subset of R^n, V : R^n -> R^l a map that is C^1 on U, eta : R^n -> R a C^1 function on R^n with compact support, tsupport(eta) contained in U and eta >= 0, and c in R^l. Assume that the integral over R^n of A[DV(x)][D zeta(x)] is 0 for every C^1 compactly supported zeta : R^n -> R^l with tsupport(zeta) contained in U. Then the lower Lebesgue integral over R^n of ofReal(eta(x)^2 ||DV(x)||^2) is at most ofReal(4 Lam^2/lam^2) times the lower Lebesgue integral over R^n of ofReal(||V(x) - c||^2 ||D eta(x)||^2). Values are in [0, infinity].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (lam Lam : ℝ) (A : (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (V : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (η : Rn n → ℝ) (c : Rn ℓ), 0 < lam → (∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, lam * ‖P‖ ^ 2 ≤ A P P) → (∀ P Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |A P Q| ≤ Lam * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖) → IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 V U → ContDiff ℝ 1 η → HasCompactSupport η → tsupport η ⊆ U → (∀ x, 0 ≤ η x) → (∀ ζ : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ U → ∫ x, A (fderiv ℝ V x) (fderiv ℝ ζ x) = 0) → ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (η x ^ 2 * ‖fderiv ℝ V x‖ ^ 2) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (4 * Lam ^ 2 / lam ^ 2) * ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (‖V x - c‖ ^ 2 * ‖fderiv ℝ η x‖ ^ 2)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4 and 5 of the parent proof (expansion and absorption) and the first part of step 6 (passage from integrals to lower integrals). Here they are carried out for an arbitrary admissible cutoff eta and an arbitrary open set U. The parent proof uses U = B_{2 rho}(y) and its particular eta. The proof uses the sibling lemma test_function (Lean: Submission.dohr_eb_sch_cacc_test_function).
Notation. L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm. A[P][Q] is the value of the continuous bilinear form A, so Q -> A[P][Q] is a continuous linear form on L. DV(x) := fderiv R V x and D eta(x) := fderiv R eta x. For v in R^l and a linear form p on R^n, v (x) p in L is h -> p(h) v; in Lean this is p.smulRight v, and its operator norm is ||p|| ||v|| (ContinuousLinearMap.norm_smulRight_apply). All integrals are over R^n with Lebesgue measure.
1. The test function. Let zeta := eta^2 (V - c). By test_function, applied to U, V, eta and c (U is open, V is C^1 on U, eta is C^1 with compact support, tsupport(eta) is contained in U), zeta is C^1 on R^n, has compact support, and tsupport(zeta) is contained in U. Moreover D zeta(x) = eta(x)^2 DV(x) + 2 eta(x) (V(x) - c) (x) D eta(x) for every x. By the hypothesis on V, the integral of h is 0, where h(x) := A[DV(x)][D zeta(x)].
2. The integrands. Put g1(x) := eta(x)^2 ||DV(x)||^2 and g3(x) := ||V(x) - c||^2 ||D eta(x)||^2.
(a) Continuity on U. DV is continuous on U, because V is C^1 on the open set U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). V is continuous on U. D eta and D zeta are continuous on R^n, because eta and zeta are C^1. A is continuous. So h, g1 and g3 are continuous on U.
(b) Supports. If x is not in tsupport(zeta), then zeta vanishes near x, so D zeta(x) = 0 and h(x) = A[DV(x)][0] = 0. If x is not in tsupport(eta), then eta(x) = 0 and D eta(x) = 0, so g1(x) = g3(x) = 0. Taking closures, tsupport(h) is contained in tsupport(zeta), which is contained in U. Likewise tsupport(g1) and tsupport(g3) are contained in tsupport(eta), which is contained in U.
(c) Global continuity and integrability. Let f be continuous on the open set U with tsupport(f) contained in U. Then f is continuous on R^n: at points of U by (a), and at points outside tsupport(f) because f vanishes near them (ContinuousOn.continuous_of_tsupport_subset). So h, g1 and g3 are continuous on R^n. Their tsupports are closed subsets of the compact sets tsupport(zeta) and tsupport(eta), so they have compact support. A continuous function with compact support is Lebesgue integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). Hence h, g1 and g3 are integrable.
3. Expansion. Fix x, and put P := DV(x) and W := (V(x) - c) (x) D eta(x). By the derivative formula of step 1 and the linearity of Q -> A[P][Q],
h(x) = eta(x)^2 A[P][P] + 2 eta(x) A[P][W].
In the notation of the parent proof this is f1 + 2 f2.
4. Pointwise lower bound. Put a := eta(x) ||P|| and b := ||V(x) - c|| ||D eta(x)||. Then a >= 0 because eta >= 0, b >= 0, g1(x) = a^2 and g3(x) = b^2.
(a) Legendre condition: eta(x)^2 A[P][P] >= eta(x)^2 lam ||P||^2 = lam a^2.
(b) Bound: ||W|| = ||D eta(x)|| ||V(x) - c|| = b, so A[P][W] >= -|A[P][W]| >= -Lam ||P|| b. Multiplying by 2 eta(x) >= 0 gives 2 eta(x) A[P][W] >= -2 Lam a b.
(c) Young's inequality: (lam/2) a^2 + (2 Lam^2/lam) b^2 - 2 Lam a b = (lam a - 2 Lam b)^2 / (2 lam) >= 0. This holds for every real Lam, because lam > 0.
Adding (a) and (b) and then using (c):
h(x) >= lam a^2 - 2 Lam a b >= lam a^2 - (lam/2) a^2 - (2 Lam^2/lam) b^2 = (lam/2) g1(x) - (2 Lam^2/lam) g3(x).
5. Absorption. All functions in step 4 are integrable, by step 2. Integrating the pointwise bound and using that the integral of h is 0 (step 1):
(lam/2) (integral of g1) - (2 Lam^2/lam) (integral of g3) <= integral of h = 0.
Since lam > 0, multiplying by 2/lam gives
integral of g1 <= (4 Lam^2/lam^2) (integral of g3).
This is the parent's chain lam (integral of g1) <= integral of f1 = -2 (integral of f2) <= 2 Lam (integral of g2) <= (lam/2) (integral of g1) + (2 Lam^2/lam) (integral of g3). Here the pointwise inequalities are combined before integrating, so only h, g1 and g3 need to be integrable. The absorbed quantity, the integral of g1, is finite.
6. Lower integrals. g1 and g3 are integrable and nonnegative. Hence the lower integral of ofReal(g1) equals ofReal(integral of g1), and the lower integral of ofReal(g3) equals ofReal(integral of g3) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal). ofReal is monotone, and ofReal(r s) = ofReal(r) ofReal(s) when r >= 0. Using step 5:
lower integral of ofReal(eta^2 ||DV||^2) = ofReal(integral of g1) <= ofReal((4 Lam^2/lam^2) (integral of g3)) = ofReal(4 Lam^2/lam^2) * ofReal(integral of g3) = ofReal(4 Lam^2/lam^2) * (lower integral of ofReal(||V - c||^2 ||D eta||^2)).
This is the claim. QED
